message.content:
Inspect /workspace/Maekfile.js and /workspace/src/main.cpp (or equivalent entry point) plus /workspace/src/test.cpp if it exists.
Report:
1. The exact build command and where the output binary lands.
2. The exact command-line invocation to run tests, including how to filter by test-name prefix (e.g. running only "a2.l1" tests).
3. Whether tests are compiled into the main Scotty3D binary or a separate binary.
Do NOT run a full build (it is slow); just read the files. You may run '/workspace/Scotty3D --help' to see flags.
Return raw technical notes.

- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
```
=== 1. BUILD ===

Build system: Maek (node-based), single file /workspace/Maekfile.js
Command (run from repo root):
    cd /workspace && node Maekfile.js
Useful flags (parsed by Maekfile.js itself, before targets):
    -jN   max parallel jobs (default = os.cpus().length + 1)
    -v    verbose (prints full compile/link commands)
    -q    quit on first error (default: builds as much as possible)
    --    separator before target names
    e.g.  node Maekfile.js -j8 -q

Default target (Maekfile.js:24):
    maek.TARGETS = ["Scotty3D" + (windows ? ".exe" : "")]

Output binary lands at repo root:
    /workspace/Scotty3D            (linux/macos; no suffix)
    /workspace/Scotty3D.exe        (windows)
Rationale: maek.LINK(objs, 'Scotty3D', opts) -> exeFile = exeFileBase + options.exeSuffix,
with NO objPrefix applied (objPrefix 'objs/' applies only to .o files). Confirmed by the
existing /workspace/Scotty3D binary (118 MB, ELF).

Intermediates: /workspace/objs/{src,tests,deps}/**.o
Build cache:   /workspace/maek-cache.json (content-hash based; delete it + objs/ to force
               a full rebuild). Incremental rebuilds only recompile changed TUs, but the
               final link of Scotty3D is always ~expensive.
Compiler (linux): g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Werror -g -O2   <-- note -Werror: any warning in
               your changed file fails the build.
Side-effect target: /workspace/README-SDL.txt is COPY'd from nest-libs and is a hard
               dependency of the Scotty3D link (Scotty3D_options.depends = [...copies]).

=== 2. RUNNING TESTS ===

Tests are run through the main binary via the --run-tests option (src/main.cpp:52):
    args.add_option("--run-tests", tests_prefix, "Run all tests starting with prefix", true);
    tests_option->expected(0, 1);      // arg is OPTIONAL

Invocations (from /workspace):
    ./Scotty3D --run-tests                 # run ALL registered tests (empty prefix)
    ./Scotty3D --run-tests a2.l1           # run only tests whose name contains "a2.l1"
    ./Scotty3D --run-tests a2.l1.flip_edge.basic.simple    # run exactly one test
    ./Scotty3D --run-tests a2              # whole assignment
Absolute form: /workspace/Scotty3D --run-tests a2.l1

Matching semantics (IMPORTANT, src/test.cpp:39-59):
  - It is a SUBSTRING match, not an anchored prefix:  test.first.find(prefix) != npos.
    So "flip_edge" matches too, and "l1" would match any name containing "l1".
  - Both the registered name and the supplied filter are lowercased (to_lower), so the
    filter is case-insensitive.
  - Test names are the string passed to the Test ctor, e.g.
      Test test_a2_l1_flip_edge_basic_simple("a2.l1.flip_edge.basic.simple", [](){...});
    Names are dotted: <assignment>.<task>.<op>.<case>, e.g. "a2.l1.flip_edge.edge.boundary",
    "a3.task3.bvh.hit.empty", "a0.task2.example.always_passes".
  - Tests live in a std::map<std::string, std::function<void()>> => run in alphabetical order.

Exit codes (verified by running the existing binary):
    0  -> all matched tests passed
    1  -> at least one matched test FAILED
    0  -> ZERO tests matched the filter (silent false-positive; run_tests returns
          failed==0). Always check the "Running N tests including '<prefix>'" header /
          "PASSED N tests" line to confirm N > 0.
  Test::ignored is counted separately and does NOT cause a nonzero exit.

Sample output (real, from ./Scotty3D --run-tests a2.l1):
    Running 2 tests including 'a2.l1':
    [1/2] a2.l1.flip_edge.basic.simple... FAILED
        flip_edge rejected operation!
    [2/2] a2.l1.flip_edge.edge.boundary... PASSED
    PASSED 1 tests.
    FAILED 1 tests.
  Output uses ANSI color escapes; pipe through `sed -r 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g'` if parsing.
  Tests run headless — no GUI/window is created when --run-tests is passed (main.cpp
  returns immediately after Test::run_tests, before any Platform/GUI init).

=== 3. SEPARATE TEST BINARY? ===

NO. Tests are compiled INTO the single Scotty3D binary. There is exactly one maek.LINK
call in Maekfile.js. Maekfile.js:229-256:

    function allTests(dir = "tests") { ...recursively maek.CPP every .cpp under tests/... }
    const test_objects = allTests();
    const Scotty3D_objects = [ ...gui_objects, ...geom_objects, ...rasterizer_objects,
        ...pathtracer_objects, ...util_objects, ...platform_objects, ...scene_objects,
        ...deps_objects, ...test_objects,
        maek.CPP("src/app.cpp"), maek.CPP("src/main.cpp"), maek.CPP("src/test.cpp") ];
    const Scotty3D_exe = maek.LINK(Scotty3D_objects, 'Scotty3D', Scotty3D_options);

Registration mechanism: each tests/**/*.cpp declares file-scope `Test` globals whose ctor
(src/test.cpp:32) inserts into a function-local static map. Because they're in the link's
object list directly (not a static lib), the globals are not stripped.

Consequence: ANY change to src/ requires the full `node Maekfile.js` relink before tests
reflect it — there is no cheap test-only build. Conversely, adding a new .cpp under
/workspace/tests/ is auto-discovered by allTests() at configure time; no Maekfile edit needed.

=== TEST INVENTORY / PATHS ===
/workspace/tests/a0/  a1/  a2/  a3/  a4/   (files named test.<name>.cpp)
113 `Test test_*` registrations total.
a2 files: test.a2.g1..g3, go1..go3, l1..l4, lx1..lx8, global.mix, local.mix
/workspace/agent_tests/ exists but is EMPTY and is NOT scanned by allTests() (which is
hardcoded to dir="tests"). Dropping a .cpp there will NOT be compiled or linked.

Key file paths:
  /workspace/Maekfile.js          (targets @ 24, allTests @ 228-241, objects @ 243-256, LINK @ 288)
  /workspace/src/main.cpp         (--run-tests option @ 52-53, dispatch @ 76-83)
  /workspace/src/test.cpp         (Test ctor @ 32, run_tests @ 39-88, to_lower @ 23)
  /workspace/src/test.h           (Test class, Test::error / Test::ignored, differs() helpers,
                                   Test::differs_eps = 0.001f, check_constant_time/log_time/
                                   linear_time/loglinear_time complexity assertions)
  /workspace/Scotty3D             (prebuilt binary present, dated Aug 14 14:26)
```
